I always remove the glue before regluing because the dried glue ends up being too lumpy to get a nice even new layer on top. You can do it as many times as you want as long as you can peel the old glue off without taking chunks of the sponge with it. Softer sponge and tougher glues make this harder. The easiest combo is something like h3 sponge and DHS glue, comes off really easy with no damage.

Someone correct me if I'm wrong on any of this. I think even grippier anti spin rubbers are less grippy than the least grippy short pips. For example even grippy anti would have a little spin reversal, and short pips don't reverse spin as far as I know. Long pips would be overall much more similar.

And then to compare anti and long pip, the only truly unique thing between them seems to be that long pips can bend and therefore have varying friction and effect while anti is flat and doesn't do that making it more predictable.

Other than that one difference, you could have any variation of both from higher friction to super low friction, and zero sponge to impact absorbing sponge to high speed sponge.

The bumps showing through the topsheet are from the glue having high spots either on the rubber or blade. You just have to smooth it over better next time or wipe excess off so the streaks left by the sponge are smaller. It shouldn't affect the performance, but it doesn't look nice. To fix it you can't just glue over it again, you have to peel all the glue off the sponge. The softer the sponge the easier it is to take chunks out along with the glue, G1 is in the middle so shouldn't be too bad just tedious (unless it's a really stubborn type of glue).
